summary: This Game Theory opening lecture is already-public method and atlas evidence: Jiang uses the dating game to define players, rules, and incentives; show that the real reward may be status rather than sex or procreation; and turn fertility into a civilizational signal with split-before-promotion forecast pressure.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: a game has players, rules or constraints, and incentives, but the real game may be status rather than the announced biological or romantic game.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The public Game Theory page already uses this source as the opening definition spine and the episode read already exposes strong source marks; no read-JSON repair is needed.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: fertility becomes status when rank incentives make children either an obstacle to status or a proof of patriotism, religion, and collective survival.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The atlas root already carries fertility-as-status as a durable relation, and the episode read already links exact dating/fertility marks to it.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Already public: keep this source as the method origin where Jiang defines game theory as players, rules or constraints, and incentives, then warns that irrational-looking behavior becomes rational once the analyst names the actual payoff.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Game Theory owns the method and payoff correction. Love and Human Heart own relation when love recognizes another person; Nation and Prediction own political-body and dated forecast branches if later promoted.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Already public: keep the superstructure section grounded in this source, where demographics, economics, culture, politics, religion, technology, and competition change the same mating desire into different games across villages, arranged marriage, dating markets, and fertility collapse.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Do not turn this into a freestanding superstructure page from one lecture. The public Game Theory parent is still the correct home for the method.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Already public: fertility as status belongs as an atlas relation because it bridges Game Theory, Nation, Education, Love/Human Heart, and Prediction without becoming a standalone topic page.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: The atlas relation is enough for now. It names a bridge across concepts while preserving Game Theory as the method page and Prediction as the only place for dated future-status claims.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use only as secondary course-method support: Jiang says education should make students thoughtful, moral, curious, imaginative, and able to analyze themselves and the world, but this source's active lens pressure is the game-theory method rather than school as an institution.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Education owns soul formation when school, tests, authority, trust, and compliance are the operative machinery. Here education is the course frame for Game Theory.

new_lens_seeds.title: Fertility As Status Game
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: A society's fertility can rise or collapse depending on whether status rewards children, family, patriotism, and religious duty or rewards individual display, upward matching, money, followers, and escape from family obligation.
new_lens_seeds.why_reusable: The mechanism can compare demographic collapse, pronatalist-policy failure, nation formation, religion, immigration, Israel, East Asia, and civilizational lifecycle arguments, but the current public atlas relation and Game Theory parent already carry the source.
new_lens_seeds.boundary_note: Do not create a standalone public child from this source alone. Reopen only if later fertility/demography sources produce enough dated fan-in and navigation pressure that the atlas relation no longer carries the mechanism.

chronology_notes.note: This is the first Game Theory classroom source in the published sequence and supplies the public definition spine before later January 2026 school, marshmallow, immigration, and world-game lectures elaborate institutional and geopolitical variants.
Jiang states that the displayed fertility/GDP data is 2024 data, preserving a concrete chronology marker for later demographic or prediction review.

The lecture frames Israel, South Korea, China, the West, Saudi Arabia, and immigration as comparative fertility/status cases; later work should keep these branches separate rather than collapsing them into one demographic forecast.

canon_candidates.claim: Jiang predicts that long-horizon civilizational power will favor societies where wealthy, well-educated women still choose children, naming Israel as the key wealthy high-tech above-replacement case and South Korea, China, and the West as severe collapse-pressure cases.
canon_candidates.boundary_note: Before ledger work, split Israel above-replacement fertility, South Korea aging/collapse, China population decline, Western immigration offset, Saudi oil-welfare outlier, and 50-year/100-year horizons into separately falsifiable records.

next_actions.note: Do not create standalone Dating Game, The Dating Game That Eats Civilization, Fertility As Status, Status Game, Superstructure, Israel Rules The Future, South Korea Zombie Society, Pronatalist Policy Failure, Wealthy Women Choose Children, or Civilizational Fertility pages from this source alone.

No immediate public Game Theory or atlas prose is needed: the source already supports the Game Theory definition spine, superstructure/status sections, the atlas fertility-status relation, and episode-to-lens links.
If forecast work follows, split the fertility/status family by country, indicator, date, and horizon before canon or ledger promotion; do not score the whole demographic thesis as one item.

If the fertility/status bridge outgrows the atlas relation, run a concept-scoped boundary review comparing Game Theory #1, Immigration Trap, Nation demographic pressure, Gerontocracy, Education/status pages, and any later Israel/Pax Judaica demographic sources before creating public prose.
